facts.fact: DPI Africa reports that at Nassarawo Primary School, Jimeta-Yola, Adamawa State, the Primary 3B teacher marks about 50 pupils' attendance each day by hand in a paper register, keeping one copy at school and one at home, and lost nearly a term's record when the register got wet; undated, so the document's published date is used.

The chief executive of Data Science Nigeria told DPI Africa that several schools in Nigeria, including some public tertiary institutions, still rely heavily on manual recordkeeping; undated, so the document's published date is used.

systems.tiers: principals carry the forms to local government offices; many rural schools report slowly or not at all

systems.country_label: national Education Management Information System (EMIS); DHIS2 EMIS
systems.owner: a consortium led by HISP Nigeria and UNICEF, with state ministries
systems.tiers: being rolled out in twelve states including Adamawa; local education authorities trained to enter enrolment, attendance and infrastructure data on tablets and smartphones; Bauchi supervisors practised uploading school census data
launched 2024; in use in UBEC's inspection and monitoring, nationwide adoption still scaling up
unveiled as a single platform of education data across basic and tertiary levels, meant to use the national identity number for student tracking

systems.owner: Data Science Nigeria, funded by the Gates Foundation
systems.tiers: piloted in Edo State; 1.9 million paper certificates secured

systems.platform: routers and devices for digital learning
systems.owner: UNICEF with telecoms operators and the Federal Ministry of Education
systems.tiers: more than 1,000 public schools connected by early 2025

note: The DHIS2 EMIS rollout is described as entry by local education authorities and the upload of school census data, with no entry by schools during the year, so it is a census; the article's wish for a teacher's attendance app is its own, not a system in use.
